cards.text: Isaiah the prophet is passing along a message from the LORD, and this one is addressed to Babylon, the great empire of the Chaldeans. The LORD speaks to her like royalty: 'O Virgin Daughter of Babylon.' But friend, He is NOT here to fluff her pillows.

cards.question: The LORD tells the Daughter of Babylon to go down and sit in the ___, with no throne.
The LORD says Babylon will keep being called tender and delicate.

cards.text: Then the princess gets a job change, and it is NOT a promotion. The LORD tells her to take millstones, which is like the CEO walking in Monday morning and getting handed a MOP.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell the Daughter of Babylon to do with the millstones?

cards.text: She's told to remove her veil and wade through the streams. The LORD says her shame will be exposed.

cards.question: The LORD tells Babylon He will take vengeance and spare no one.

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of the message, a short line about 'Our Redeemer' breaks in. It says 'the LORD of Hosts is His name.'

cards.question: In the line that breaks into the message to Babylon, 'Our Redeemer' is called the Holy One of which people?

cards.text: Back to the LORD's words for Babylon: 'Sit in silence and go into darkness, O Daughter of the Chaldeans.' Friend, that's not a quiet night in, that's somebody closing the drawer on you.

cards.question: The LORD tells the Daughter of the Chaldeans she'll lose a title. What will she no longer be called?

cards.text: Then the LORD explains how His own people ended up in Babylon's hands. He was angry with His people, and He placed them under Babylon's control.

cards.question: Once God's people were under Babylon's control, how did Babylon treat them?
Babylon went easy on the elderly among God's people.

cards.text: And Babylon? Babylon's talking like that crown is GLUED on.

cards.question: Babylon said, 'I will be ___ forever.'
Babylon thought carefully about where all of this would lead.

cards.text: Now the LORD gives Babylon a new nickname: 'O lover of luxury who sits securely.' And then He tells us exactly what she says to herself.

cards.question: What does Babylon, the lover of luxury who sits securely, say to herself?

answers.text: There is one greater than me

cards.text: She's so sure of herself, friend, she names two kinds of grief that will never touch her.

cards.question: Babylon says she will never be a ___ or know the loss of ___.

cards.text: The LORD says those two things will overtake her in a moment, in a single day. That's not a slow bake, friend, that's the timer going off before you've even shut the oven door.

cards.question: Babylon's many sorceries and powerful spells will keep those losses away.

cards.text: Babylon felt secure in her wickedness, sure she had it all figured out, and said, 'No one sees me.' That's me hiding a cookie behind my back with crumbs ALL over my mustache.

cards.question: The LORD says Babylon's ___ and knowledge led her astray.

cards.text: But disaster is coming, a calamity Babylon will be unable to ward off. And it will hit suddenly and unexpectedly.

cards.question: Disaster is coming for Babylon. What does the LORD say she won't know how to do with it?

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Babylon to take her stand with her spells and sorceries, the ones she's worn herself out with since her youth. And He adds, 'Perhaps you will succeed; perhaps you will inspire terror!'

cards.question: The LORD already said Babylon can't ward off this calamity. So when He says 'Perhaps you will succeed,' what is He doing?

cards.text: Next the LORD says Babylon is wearied by her many counselors, the astrologers who observe the stars and monthly predict her fate. My boy Berry watched the stars every night too, but he NEVER sold anybody a monthly forecast.

cards.question: The LORD tells Babylon to let her counselors come forward now and save her.

cards.text: Then the LORD shows what those astrologers really are.

cards.question: Babylon's astrologers are like ___ that the fire burns up.
When the fire comes for Babylon's astrologers, there will be coals left over to warm them.

cards.text: Last, the LORD tells Babylon what they are to her, those she has labored and traded with since her youth.

cards.question: What does the LORD say each of those Babylon has labored and traded with since her youth does?

cards.text: And the message ends right there, quiet as a closed drawer: not one of them can save her.

findings.problem: The phrase 'all of this' points back to earlier cards without identifying what Babylon failed to consider. The choice card does not supply that context itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never 'him,' 'that' or 'it' pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The setup says only that Babylon names two kinds of grief. It gives no basis for reasoning out 'widow' and 'children,' and losses of 'wealth' or 'kingdoms' are also plausible from the earlier cards. The baker must guess wording that has not yet been shown.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The phrase 'those losses' relies on the preceding cards rather than identifying widowhood and the loss of children in the question itself.
